To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nonresonant dissociative electron attachment cross sections for the e-H 2 system are much larger than previously assumed and that they are larger than the resonant cross sections at most incident electron energies.

(i) the dissociative electron attachment cross section of molecular hydrogen at energies from threshold up to 6 e is dominated by nonresonant processes and (ii) the cross section to the ground vibrational state of H2 is significantly smaller than that to the first excited state, in contrast to the predictions of all previous calculations.
the dissociative attachment of electrons to molecular hydrogen is dominated by nonresonant processes at all but the very lowest energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental interactions of low-energy electrons with atoms and molecules.

the development and application of new methods for the study of electron-molecule interactions and the application of those methods to problems in electron attachment, electron scattering and electron-induced chemistry and physics of gases.
the study of the interaction of low-energy electrons with molecular hydrogen, a system of great fundamental and practical importance.

the dissociative electron attachment cross sections for molecular hydrogen are dominated by nonresonant contributions, and the resonant contribution is not as important as previously believed.
the nonresonant component of cross sections for dissociative electron attachment of H2 is large, and that the resonance component is small.
nonresonant processes dominate the dissociative attachment of low-energy electrons to molecular hydrogen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are now able to calculate dissociative electron attachment cross sections to molecular hydrogen in its ground vibratical state with an accuracy of 20%.
nonresonant dissociative electron attachment has been found to be important for H2 and that this finding has implications for electron attachment to many other molecular systems.

the nonadiabated phase-matrix method, which includes both nonresonant and resonant scattering, has been shown to give a very good representation of the dissociative attachment cross sections to molecular hydrogen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for electron-molecule scattering, nonresonant processes are often more important than resonant processes, especially at low energies.
the nonresonant component to dissociative attachment cross sections is much larger than has generally been appreciated, and this component must be accounted for in any theoretical description.
nonresonant dissociative electron attachment should not be neglected in any theory of this process.
